summary: The University of Illinois site reports its status in response to RFC 116. Hardware linking its PDP-11 to the IMP worked, but trouble with the Burroughs B6500 slowed network software checkout. It expected to finish the NCP checkout by late May and be operating in June.

eli5.summary: A school tells the others its computers are plugged in but a different machine caused delays. They hope to finish in a few weeks.

subtitle: A one-paragraph status report on the University of Illinois ARPA Network connection in April 1971.

tldr.problem: RFC 116 asked for the status of the Illinois site on the network.
tldr.mechanism: J. Bouknight reports that the hardware connecting the PDP-11 system to the IMP is complete, but trouble with the Burroughs B6500 has slowed software checkout.
tldr.outcome: NCP checkout was expected by the latter part of May and the system was expected to be operational during June.

today: The unit metadata lists the status of RFC 156 as Unknown. It updates RFC 116 and has no obsoleting or updating RFCs. It is a historical status report.

sections.title: Where the Illinois Site Stood
sections.content:
As of 26 April, the Illinois Site had complete operational hardware connecting the PDP-11 system with the IMP. The report is a response to RFC 116.

Final checkout of the operating system plus the network control program (NCP) for the PDP-11 had been seriously curtailed because of much trouble with the Burroughs B6500 computer.
sections.eli5: The wires are connected and working, but the programs that use them are not finished being tested.

sections.title: What Was Expected Next
sections.content: Two expectations are listed. First, checkout of the NCP by the latter part of May. Second, installation of the PDP-11 system in Paoli, PA, which is the operating link between Illinois and Burroughs, so that the system would be operational during June.
sections.eli5: They planned to finish testing by late May and move the machine to a partner location so it works in June.

sections.title: Why a Status Note Mattered
sections.content: The note has no protocol content. It is a snapshot of a site joining the early network, and it shows that connecting a host involved more than the IMP hardware: an operating system and an NCP also had to be working before the site could take part.
sections.eli5: Plugging in is only the first step. The computer also needs the right programs before it can talk to others.

references.text: The RFC to which this status report responds, RFC 116.
